rationales.quote: So one ring - talk to me
rationales.explanation: Mark asks for clarification about how the single-ring product works.

rationales.quote: the ring will be connected to all of the devices
rationales.explanation: Mark checks his understanding of the ring's operational connection to household devices.

rationales.quote: a house would have this all throughout any room that they want
rationales.explanation: Mark clarifies the proposed in-home installation and point-and-click operating model.

rationales.quote: what's the perspective on wearing the ring constantly versus making it something that's kind of like a television remote?
rationales.explanation: Mark asks about user acceptance of the ring's intended wearing pattern and form factor.

rationales.quote: on the B2B side, you're targeting retirement homes
rationales.explanation: Mark identifies retirement homes as the proposed initial customer segment and seeks confirmation.

rationales.quote: the value prop to them is, hey, we'll install this ring in all of your rooms
rationales.explanation: Mark checks the B2B sales proposition and deployment approach for retirement homes.

rationales.quote: It didn't - it just didn't work well.
rationales.explanation: Mark reports a poor personal experience with a comparable consumer product, providing a negative experience-based comparator.

rationales.quote: It just did not function well.
rationales.explanation: Mark reiterates his negative personal experience with the comparable product.

rationales.quote: I think maybe it has tapered off a little bit.
rationales.explanation: Mark characterizes the analogous Oura form factor as having possibly weakened in adoption or momentum and asks what Lotus can learn from it.

rationales.quote: No one here is wearing an Oura Ring.
rationales.explanation: Mark points to the lack of visible use of a comparable ring product as a negative adoption signal.

rationales.quote: I'm really impressed with your control of this business.
rationales.explanation: Mark positively assesses Dhaval's command of the business.

rationales.quote: I really like it.
rationales.explanation: Mark explicitly states that he likes the product or opportunity.

rationales.quote: It's gonna be too early for us. We want to see a little bit more progress on the product.
rationales.explanation: Mark declines because the company is too early and has not yet demonstrated enough product progress.

rationales.quote: this could catch on like wildfire, and when there's another round, that might be interesting for us
rationales.explanation: Mark sees substantial future adoption potential and links it to possible interest in a later round.

rationales.quote: He was super impressive.
rationales.explanation: In later commentary, Mark gives a strong positive assessment of the founder.

rationales.quote: He did great.
rationales.explanation: In later commentary, Mark reiterates his positive assessment of the founder's performance.

merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: So one ring - talk to me
rationales.explanation: Mark asks for clarification about how the single-ring product operates.

rationales.quote: the ring will be connected to all of the devices like this
rationales.explanation: Mark checks his understanding of how the ring connects to household devices.

rationales.quote: a house would have this all throughout any room that they want
rationales.explanation: Mark seeks confirmation about the proposed in-home deployment and operating model.

rationales.quote: what's the perspective on wearing the ring constantly versus making it something that's kind of like a television remote?
rationales.explanation: Mark asks about user acceptance of the ring's wearing pattern and form factor.

rationales.quote: on the B2B side, you're targeting retirement homes
rationales.explanation: Mark checks whether retirement homes are the proposed initial customer segment.

rationales.quote: the value prop to them is, hey, we'll install this ring in all of your rooms
rationales.explanation: Mark clarifies the B2B value proposition and deployment approach.

rationales.quote: I totally bought one. It didn't - it just didn't work well.
rationales.explanation: Mark cites a negative personal experience with a comparable product as a relevant point of comparison.

rationales.quote: It just did not function well.
rationales.explanation: Mark reiterates his negative personal experience with the comparable product.

rationales.quote: I think maybe it has tapered off a little bit.
rationales.explanation: Mark raises a possible decline in adoption or momentum for the analogous Oura form factor and asks what Lotus can learn from it.

rationales.quote: No one here is wearing an Oura Ring.
rationales.explanation: Mark points to the lack of visible use of a comparable ring product as an adoption concern.

rationales.quote: I'm really impressed with your control of this business.
rationales.explanation: Mark positively assesses Dhaval's command and operational control of the company.

rationales.quote: I really like it.
rationales.explanation: Mark expresses a positive reaction to the product or opportunity.

rationales.quote: It's gonna be too early for us. We want to see a little bit more progress on the product.
rationales.explanation: Mark declines because the company has not yet demonstrated enough product progress for his investment.

rationales.quote: when you do go to market, this could catch on like wildfire, and when there's another round, that might be interesting for us
rationales.explanation: Mark sees substantial future adoption potential and links that prospect to possible interest in a later round.

rationales.quote: He was super impressive.
rationales.explanation: In later commentary, Mark gives a strong positive assessment of the founder.

rationales.quote: He did great.
rationales.explanation: In later commentary, Mark reiterates his positive assessment of the founder's performance.

Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.
